newsitem.title: UK: American Airlines, BA plan cooperation - paper.
newsitem.headline: American Airlines, BA plan cooperation - paper.

text.p: American Airlines and British Airways are considering ways to start cooperating despite continued regulatory hurdles to a formal alliance, a British newspaper said on Tuesday.
American, part of AMR Corp, and BA could start sharing facilities at Britain's Heathrow airport and American's U.S. hubs and could begin joint marketing initiatives, the Independent newspaper said.
The proposed alliance has come under fire from regulators.

Britain's Office of Fair Trading said in December it would clear the alliance if the companies gave up 168 weekly landing and taking off slots at Heathrow, but European Competition Commissioner Karel van Miert has said the trading of slots is not acceptable.
BA executives said there were a number of areas where the airlines could cooperate before their alliance was given the all-clear by regulators, the Independent said.
British Airways on Monday reported record profits as it celebrated 10 years in the private sector.
